rounds.label: root cause found: the sensor is band-limited near 50 Hz
rounds.headline: 796 Hz of samples carrying 50 Hz of content — the strike-vs-ring difference is filtered out before it reaches us
rounds.biggest_gap: Power above 100 Hz is 9-10 orders down, at numerical noise. A knuckle strike is broadband to several kHz; none of it arrives. This explains all eleven failed mechanisms, and why rise time measured 13.8 vs 12.6 ms (that was the filter, not the taps). The service exposes ReportInterval and BatchInterval only - 27 of 29 candidate bandwidth/filter/ODR keys return nothing, so the ceiling is not ours to move.

rounds.label: ring-to-strike: what actually predicts a working surface
rounds.headline: Tap size, noise floor and SNR do not predict lap detection — the ring does
rounds.biggest_gap: Across four lap sessions tap amplitude (0.032-0.036 g), noise floor and decay time were identical and SNR ran BACKWARDS (the 100% session had the worst). What tracked detection was how much of the first strike was still ringing when the second landed: 0.30/0.38/0.42 gave 95/90/100%, and 0.61 gave 80%. Calibration now measures it and tells the user, since it is the one thing they can act on by changing posture.

rounds.label: one command for the missing recordings
rounds.headline: The eight ungraded checks now have a 28-minute script, guarded by a test
rounds.biggest_gap: Eight held-out checks read 'no typing sessions' or 'no confound sessions', so the harness returns INCOMPLETE rather than a verdict and the make-or-break metric has never been graded out of sample. bin/record-for-the-bar.sh records exactly those plus a 60-gesture lap deck. Writing the guard for it caught a stale --note flag in RESUME.md that the CLI rejects outright.

rounds.label: the ring carries what the noise floor did not
rounds.headline: Surface detection was the wrong question — the ring is measurable and is what predicts detection
rounds.biggest_gap: Ring-to-strike reads desk 0.20-0.29, soft 0.18-0.34, lap 0.30-0.61, overlapping in only two of ten sessions; the noise floor reads 0.00011/0.00014/0.00012 and separates nothing. Ten sessions is too few for automatic switching, but the surface was never the thing worth knowing: a lap that does not ring works (0.42, 100%) and a lap that does fails (0.61, 80%). Calibration reports the ring directly.
